pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:214 readStrip calls countEvents once per day in a loop, so one render of the page issues about 84 count queries where one grouped aggregate (count per day and actor kind) would answer the strip in a single round trip. The technique calls exactly this loop a design failure of the surface.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:214 One count query per strip day (STRIP_PAST=84). readFacets also loops countEvents once per held project. The kernel offers no grouped per-day count.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:6 The screen has no SQL. Every read goes through the kernel's named queryEvents and countEvents in one read module that the page, the actions and the JSONL route all share.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:142 Page, Facets and Strip are read-only projections shaped for the screen. Nothing is written back.
tests/next-server/ledger-read.test.ts:24 The read module is tested against a real in-memory kernel store, not a mock.

pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/library/query.ts:85 rowOf casts the closed-vocabulary text columns (kind, state, origin, source) straight to the domain enum, and library_items.state carries no CHECK, so an unknown variant passes through as if it were a member. This is the silent third option row-mapping bans.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/library/query.ts:85 The serialized face column is parsed through a zod door and throws on failure, which is correct. The enum columns are unchecked casts.

packages/kernel/src/library/clauses.ts:53 A dynamic identifier reaches SQL only through the COLUMN_GROUPS allowlist. Values are bound. FTS escaping lives in one place (core.ts ftsExpression). ORDER BY comes from a closed map.
packages/kernel/src/library/query.ts:115 Page rows and chips (chipsFor) are fetched as membership sets keyed into a Map. There is no per-row query.
packages/kernel/src/library/write.ts:86 Row writes compose inside the caller's Tx. upsertItems and actOnItem own one transaction each, and the mark commits with its event.
packages/kernel/src/library/schema.ts:8 A stored read model with a named recomputation (lib/library/project.ts). Digest-keyed upsert makes a re-projection idempotent.
packages/kernel/test/library.test.ts:24 Tested on a real SQLite kernel.

pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:119 An app-level adapter in lib/ writes raw SQL against tables that packages/kernel/src/spend owns (publish.ts does the same against `parts`). The query language leaks outside the kernel's store modules, and 'who reads spend_rows' is no longer a directory listing.

techniques.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:119 spend_rows, spend_reservations and spend_counters are kernel tables (packages/kernel/src/spend/v1Port.ts) queried directly from lib/ledger. publish.ts:134 queries `parts` the same way.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:120 Values are bound parameters. No interpolation of external text.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/articles.ts:141 The corrupt-row policy is visible degradation: an undecodable v1 record is skipped with its id and the door's reason, carried on Projection.skipped.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:118 Rows, holds and counters are read in one read transaction, so the tally checks a consistent snapshot.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:29 The adapters are pure projections that never write back to a v1 store. spend deliberately bypasses a meter read that would prune and write.
